note: The machine-readable half of docs/art/ASSET-SPEC.md's budget section. Every number here is either measured from a named on-disk source or explicitly marked provisional. tests/asset-budget.test.mjs enforces it and fails when the prose and this file disagree.

baseline.measuredBy: npm run build, then tools/asset-budget.mjs measure
baseline.sourcemapNote: package.json build.files excludes dist/**/*.map, so sourcemaps are built but never shipped and are excluded from every ceiling below.

ceilings.shippedTotalWhy: 24 MiB = the 1.85 MiB code baseline plus the 20 MiB asset allowance plus ~2 MiB of slack; a 24 MiB cold download is ~20 s on a 10 Mbit line, which is the largest first-launch wait this game's scope justifies.
ceilings.codeWhy: 2.25 MiB = the 1.85 MiB measured code baseline plus ~22% growth headroom: ordinary feature work will not trip it, a doubling or an accidentally-bundled dependency will.
ceilings.assetWhy: 20 MiB is the ceiling on the TOTAL shortlist across all art-search issues combined, not a per-asset allowance: one 2K HDRI (~4 MB KTX2), a small PBR set (~8 x 1K, ~8 MB), and a few meshes (~4 MB) fit with room, and anything larger is a decision rather than a purchase.
ceilings.vramWhy: PROVISIONAL. No atlas-scale VRAM reasoning exists in this repo to derive from, so 512 MiB is set as the resident-texture headroom that keeps the game inside a 2 GB shared-memory integrated adapter alongside the framebuffer and post stack. Replace it with a measured figure when one exists. The two checkable proxies below stand in for it meanwhile.
ceilings.gpuProxyWhy: Texture and geometry counts from the capture manifest's perf block are the only committed VRAM-adjacent measurements that exist; 96/900 is roughly +80%/+29% over the 53/700 baseline, sized so an asset pack landing wholesale is visible before a VRAM measurement exists.

frameTime.why: A CEILING, not a band. The documented '21-26 ms band' does not survive contact with the record: the committed perf runs report combat-24 medians of 16.9, 18.6, 20.0, 20.5, 21.8, 20.5 and 24.5 ms, so five of seven sit below the band's lower bound and a lower bound would fail runs that got faster. 26.0 ms keeps the documented upper bound; p95 32.0 ms sits just above the worst recorded p95 (27.1 ms) plus the run-to-run spread the same record shows.
frameTime.toleranceWhy: The record's own medians span 16.9-24.5 ms on one machine across one tree family — roughly +/-19% around the midpoint — so any ceiling tighter than about +25% over the latest recorded median (20.5 ms) would flap on run noise rather than on regressions. 26.0 ms is +27%.
frameTime.historicalWhy: The review-prose medians the whys above cite, kept here so the spec's historical citations stay allowlisted by the stray-figure sweep even as the live frameTimeRecord is re-measured and its numbers move.
